title: " Ausbildung und Gestaltung von seitlichen Baustellenzuwegungen im Längsverkehr auf BAB "
description: Im Zuge der Durchführung von Bauarbeiten müssen regelmäßig Baustellenfahrzeuge, Transportfahrzeuge und Baumaschinen in den Arbeitsbereich ein- und ausfahren. Hierfür kommen insbesondere bei langen Baustellenabschnitten Baustellenzuwegungen innerhalb der Arbeitsstelle, d. h. im Längsverkehr der Autobahn, zum Einsatz. Solche Zuwegungen führen zu zusätzlichen Konfliktpunkten mit dem fließenden Verkehr, die die Verkehrssicherheit mindern bzw. zu Störungen im Verkehrsablauf führen können. Aktuell gibt es keine Standards für die Ausbildung und Gestaltung von solchen Baustellenzuwegungen. Während Baustellenzuwegungen in Regelwerken und Arbeitsschutzvorschriften grundsätzlich berücksichtigt werden, liegen bislang nur wenige wissenschaftlich fundierte Erkenntnisse zu deren sicherer und leistungsfähiger Gestaltung vor. Ziel dieses Forschungsvorhabens ist die systematische Untersuchung von Baustellenzuwegungen innerhalb von Arbeitsstellen längerer Dauer auf BAB sowie die Erarbeitung wissenschaftlich fundierter Empfehlungen für deren Planung, Gestaltung und Betrieb. Weiterhin sollen geeignete Bewertungsmaßstäbe entwickelt werden, mit denen die Eignung unterschiedlicher Lösungen hinsichtlich Verkehrssicherheit, Verkehrsablauf und Praktikabilität beurteilt werden kann. Als Ergebnis des Forschungsvorhabens sind Handlungsempfehlungen für die Planung, Ausschreibung, Genehmigung und den Betrieb von Baustellenzuwegungen im Längsverkehr zu erarbeiten. Es sind unter anderem Vorgaben zur geeigneten Lage, Entwicklungslänge, Beschilderung und Markierung sowie zu verkehrstechnischen Maßnahmen abgeleitet werden. Zudem sollen Vorschläge für die Fortschreibung bestehender Regelwerke, Leitfäden, Verordnungen und technischer Vorschriften abgeleitet werden (z. B. RSA, VwV StVO, ZTV SA). Das Vorhaben soll einen Beitrag zur sicheren, effizienten und regelwerkskonformen Abwicklung von Arbeitsstellen längerer Dauer auf hochbelasteten Bundesautobahnen leisten.

Täten Helsingin kaupungin työllisyyspalveluliikelaitos hankkii tekoälyavusteisen tulkkauspalvelun. Tulkkauspalvelun on pystyttävä tarjoamaan tulkkausta useilla kielillä. Palvelun tulee hyödyntää tekoälyä reaaliaikaisen tulkkauksen tarjoamiseen. Tulkkauspalvelun on oltava luottamuksellinen ja yksityisyyttä suojaava (Helsingin kaupungin tietosuojavaatimukset on täytettävä ja ne toimitetaan myöhemmin erikseen). Palvelun tulee olla helppokäyttöinen niin asiakkaille kuin palvelun tarjoajille ja käyttöliittymän voi käyttää eri laitteilla (tietokone, älypuhelin, tabletti, tms.). title: Barn og unges digitale hverdag - i spennet mellom rettigheter, deltakelse, relasjoner og sosiale dynamikk
description: Formålet med forskningsprosjektet er å utvikle kunnskap om mangfoldet av barn og unges digitale hverdagsliv, og hvordan digitaliseringen påvirker deres fellesskap og muligheter for deltakelse i samfunnet. Et sentralt utgangspunkt er å belyse spenningen mellom deres rett til informasjon og deltakelse på nett på den ene siden, og retten til beskyttelse på nett på den andre. Denne spenningen gir opphav til dilemmaer i skjæringspunktet mellom individ og system, hvor hensynet til barns rettigheter må avveies mot behovet for personvern, regulering og kontroll. Videre skal prosjektet utforske dilemma knyttet til hvordan digitale medier inngår i barn og unges sosiale liv – både med jevnaldrende, foresatte, profesjonelle omsorgspersoner, og andre voksne. Digitale samhandlingsformer er integrert i relasjoner og sosiale sammenhenger, og kan bidra både positivt og negativt til tilhørighet, deltakelse og sosial dynamikk – både digitalt og analogt. Prosjektet skal derfor belyse hvorvidt og eventuelt hvordan digital samhandling former barn og unges relasjoner og sosiale dynamikker, og bidra til økt forståelse av disse prosessene og betydningen av dem. Samlet skal oppdraget bidra til økt innsikt i de relasjonelle og samfunnsmessige konsekvensene av en oppvekst der digitale og analoge arenaer er sammenvevd.

title: CivTech 12.1 - How can digital technologies assist people living with substance use issues (and their families/friends) to easily connect with trusted help and substance use support when services are unavailable?
description: Scotland has the highest drug and alcohol related death rates in the UK and Europe. People with substance use issues (PWSUI) often need help outside normal 'office' hours or from a distance from offices, and support is not uniformly available throughout Scotland. The support landscape in Scotland is fragmented, hard to navigate, and varies by locality. When support isn’t readily available (or isn’t trusted), people and their families and friends often default to emergency services or remain unsupported. As a result, those who use substances often experience avoidable crisis escalation, or remain in extremely difficult situations, and support services miss opportunities for early, harm-reducing interventions. The Preventing Harm, Promoting Recovery: Scotland’s Alcohol & Drugs Strategic Plan 2026 – 2035 specifically addresses the crucial need to tackle early intervention and widen an individual’s ‘circle of support’. This ‘circle of support’ is at the heart of this Challenge, and a successful solution would enable people to access the right support sooner, regardless of locality. It should harness the power of existing trusted services, family and community to reduce avoidable demand on emergency and NHS services – and if possible, create a ‘feedback loop’ of learning, intelligence and insight so that the overall issue can be tackled in a continually improving manner.

title: How can technology enable fast-growing digital public service providers to dynamically scale their service management capabilities as demand, complexity and customer expectations increase?
description: The Scottish Government’s Directorate for Digital is seeking an innovative service management solution to support a growing portfolio of digital services, including ScotAccount, ScotPayments, mygov.scot, Cloud Platform Services, and more. As demand, complexity and user expectations increase, we require scalable, technology-enabled approaches that can grow as our services grow, while delivering value for money. A successful solution will help ensure resilient, secure and efficient service operations, reducing risks to service quality, productivity, revenue and public trust, while supporting the future development of Scotland’s digital public services.

title: CivTech 12.5 - How can technology support multi agency processes for the protection of children in Scotland?
description: This Challenge presents an exciting opportunity to make a positive difference in protecting children in Scotland from harm, an area of the highest priority for the Scottish Cabinet and partners. Scotland’s child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities. These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families. The Scottish Government, Police Scotland and the National Social Work Agency (TBC) are seeking innovative solutions that will enable secure streamlined multi-agency information sharing for the existing IRD process, as well as providing real-time local and national data to improve child protection outcomes across Scotland.

title: CivTech 12 - Challenge 12.3 - How can we use technology to demonstrate the commercial value of circular economy business practices?
description: Zero Waste Scotland is seeking an innovative technology solution that helps businesses demonstrate the commercial value of circular economy practices and attract investment. Existing assessment tools often overlook benefits including (but not limited to) supply chain resilience, resource security, customer retention and reduced exposure to market shocks. We are looking for an intuitive, evidence-based tool that integrates the wider benefits into business and investment decisions, while generating insights to inform future support and policy development. The solution should build business and investor confidence, help accelerate adoption of circular practices and support Scotland's transition to a sustainable, circular economy.

title: CivTech 12.6 - How can technology improve living conditions and quality of life for social housing residents in Scotland?
description: Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities. While Registered Social Landlords are investing in warmer, more energy-efficient housing and responding to new regulatory requirements, fuel poverty means many vulnerable residents remain at risk, even in high-quality homes. Current approaches are often reactive and lack mechanisms to target support for those that might be the very most vulnerable, addressing issues only after harm has occurred. This Challenge seeks innovative solutions that can help registered social landlords identify where housing conditions, fuel poverty and individual vulnerability combine to create the greatest risk of harm, then translate that insight into practical, targeted action that combats these impacts, improves tenants’ health and wellbeing outcomes, protects homes and makes better use of limited housing and support resources. Solutions must be affordable at RSL scale, protect tenant privacy, and connect insight to action so that Cloch can complete investigation and repair work within statutory timescales.

title: Civtech 12 - Challenge 12.2 - How can technology enable fast-growing digital public service providers to dynamically scale their service management capabilities as demand, complexity and customer expectations increase?
description: The Scottish Government’s Directorate for Digital is seeking an innovative service management solution to support a growing portfolio of digital services, including ScotAccount, ScotPayments, mygov.scot, Cloud Platform Services, and more. As demand, complexity and user expectations increase, we require scalable, technology-enabled approaches that can grow as our services grow, while delivering value for money. A successful solution will help ensure resilient, secure and efficient service operations, reducing risks to service quality, productivity, revenue and public trust, while supporting the future development of Scotland’s digital public services.

title: CivTech 12 - Challenge 12.4 - How can technology improve both the efficiency and the patient experience in NHS transport, starting with renal services?​
description: With over 273,000 people in Scotland living with Stage 3-5 Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), including 2,000 receiving dialysis treatment, and demand expected to increase fivefold over the next decade, improvements to dialysis transport across NHS Scotland are urgently needed. Dialysis journeys account for more than 40% of all non-emergency patient transport activity, costing 9.1 million GBP annually. Yet current arrangements can be inconsistent, creating avoidable pressures for patients, providers and NHS services. NHS Scotland is seeking innovative, patient-centred and sustainable solutions that improve reliability, efficiency and patient outcomes, while reducing administrative burden and delivering better value for money.

title: CivTech 12.6 - How can technology improve living conditions and quality of life for social housing residents in Scotland?
description: Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities. While Registered Social Landlords are investing in warmer, more energy-efficient housing and responding to new regulatory requirements, fuel poverty means many vulnerable residents remain at risk, even in high-quality homes. Current approaches are often reactive and lack mechanisms to target support for those that might be the very most vulnerable, addressing issues only after harm has occurred. This Challenge seeks innovative solutions that can help registered social landlords identify where housing conditions, fuel poverty and individual vulnerability combine to create the greatest risk of harm, then translate that insight into practical, targeted action that combats these impacts, improves tenantsâ health and wellbeing outcomes, protects homes and makes better use of limited housing and support resources. Solutions must be affordable at RSL scale, protect tenant privacy, and connect insight to action so that Cloch can complete investigation and repair work within statutory timescales.

title: CivTech 12.5 - How can technology support multi agency processes for the protection of children in Scotland?
description: This Challenge presents an exciting opportunity to make a positive difference in protecting children in Scotland from harm, an area of the highest priority for the Scottish Cabinet and partners. Scotlandâs child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities. These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families. The Scottish Government, Police Scotland and the National Social Work Agency (TBC) are seeking innovative solutions that will enable secure streamlined multi-agency information sharing for the existing IRD process, as well as providing real-time local and national data to improve child protection outcomes across Scotland.

title: Civtech 12 - Challenge 12.2 - How can technology enable fast-growing digital public service providers to dynamically scale their service management capabilities as demand, complexity and customer expectations increase?
description: The Scottish Governmentâs Directorate for Digital is seeking an innovative service management solution to support a growing portfolio of digital services, including ScotAccount, ScotPayments, mygov.scot, Cloud Platform Services, and more. As demand, complexity and user expectations increase, we require scalable, technology-enabled approaches that can grow as our services grow, while delivering value for money. A successful solution will help ensure resilient, secure and efficient service operations, reducing risks to service quality, productivity, revenue and public trust, while supporting the future development of Scotlandâs digital public services.

title: CivTech 12 - Challenge 12.3 - How can we use technology to demonstrate the commercial value of circular economy business practices?
description: Zero Waste Scotland is seeking an innovative technology solution that helps businesses demonstrate the commercial value of circular economy practices and attract investment. Existing assessment tools often overlook benefits including (but not limited to) supply chain resilience, resource security, customer retention and reduced exposure to market shocks. We are looking for an intuitive, evidence-based tool that integrates the wider benefits into business and investment decisions, while generating insights to inform future support and policy development. The solution should build business and investor confidence, help accelerate adoption of circular practices and support Scotland's transition to a sustainable, circular economy.

title: CivTech 12 - Challenge 12.4 - How can technology improve both the efficiency and the patient experience in NHS transport, starting with renal services?â

title: CivTech 12.1 - How can digital technologies assist people living with substance use issues (and their families/friends) to easily connect with trusted help and substance use support when services are unavailable?
description: Scotland has the highest drug and alcohol related death rates in the UK and Europe. People with substance use issues (PWSUI) often need help outside normal 'office' hours or from a distance from offices, and support is not uniformly available throughout Scotland. The support landscape in Scotland is fragmented, hard to navigate, and varies by locality. When support isnât readily available (or isnât trusted), people and their families and friends often default to emergency services or remain unsupported. As a result, those who use substances often experience avoidable crisis escalation, or remain in extremely difficult situations, and support services miss opportunities for early, harm-reducing interventions. The Preventing Harm, Promoting Recovery: Scotlandâs Alcohol & Drugs Strategic Plan 2026 â 2035 specifically addresses the crucial need to tackle early intervention and widen an individualâs âcircle of supportâ. This âcircle of supportâ is at the heart of this Challenge, and a successful solution would enable people to access the right support sooner, regardless of locality. It should harness the power of existing trusted services, family and community to reduce avoidable demand on emergency and NHS services â and if possible, create a âfeedback loopâ of learning, intelligence and insight so that the overall issue can be tackled in a continually improving manner.

title: Modular Wind Power for Northern Operations
description: This Challenge notice is issued under the Innovation for Defence Excellence and Security (IDEaS) Program Call for Proposals (CFP) Call 006 (W7714-248676/A). Solicitation Documents reference: See bidding details section. *For additional general information on the IDEaS Program, visit: https://www.canada.ca/en/department-national-defence/programs/defence-ideas.html _____________ This challenge is open to receive proposals for Component 1a, Component 1b and Component 2. Proposed solutions that fall within technology readiness levels (TRL) 1-9 can be submitted to this challenge. Steps to apply: Step 1: read this challenge Step 2: read the Call for Proposals : See bidding details section Step 3: propose your solution here : https://defence-innovation-portal.my.site.com/ _____________ Maximum Funding and Performance Period Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge. The individual maximum contract funding available under Component 1a (TRL 1-3) is up to $250,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of up to 6 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 1b (TRL 4-5) is up to $1,500,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of 12 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 2 (TRL 6-9) is up to $5,000,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes). The period of performance will be determined at the time of contract negotiation. The maximum individual contractual funding and the maximum performance period offered under Component 3 will be determined by Canada at the time of contract negotiation. This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to contract for the total approximate funding. _____________ Challenge Details Challenge Title: W7714-248676/016 - Modular Wind Power For North Operations The Department of National Defence and Canadian Armed Forces (DND/CAF) are seeking innovative solutions to develop modular, stand-alone wind-powered electric generator systems that can be easily transported, deployed, and maintained in remote northern locations to provide reliable, clean energy under extreme cold, high-wind, and icing conditions. Background & Context The demand for electrical power and space heating in the Canadian Subarctic and High Arctic is fulfilled almost exclusively with diesel-fired generators. The DND/CAF is seeking to reduce reliance on fossil fuels for the generation of electrical power in the North to minimize operational, logistical, and environmental burdens. Wind turbines suitable for DND/CAF operations are in limited use in the North, as existing installations tend to fall outside the desired capacity range. While small units that deliver up to 6 kilowatts (kW) have been deployed in some communities, and commercial turbines typically exceed 1 megawatt (MW), there is a critical gap in the 25–100 kW range—an ideal scale for remote DND sites. In addition, northern operating conditions present major technical and environmental hurdles that must be overcome before wind turbines can be fully exploited as a source of alternative energy. Canada's far North and Arctic regions are characterized by seasonally frozen ground, deep snow, rugged terrain, permafrost, and extreme temperatures that can reach –60 degrees Celsius (°C), with frequent high winds of 80–120 kilometers per hour (km/h). Ice rimming of wind turbine blades further threatens performance and efficiency. Innovative approaches are therefore needed to adapt conventional wind-powered electric generator designs to withstand these harsh northern conditions and operate effectively under both low and high wind scenarios. Climate change adds additional complexity, as thawing and refreezing permafrost can cause buildings and foundations to sink, shift, or crack. While not the primary focus of the challenge, consideration must be given to the design of the foundations to keep the turbines level and stable despite seasonal ground movement. There is a need for wind-powered electricity generators that are logistically efficient, easy to deploy, and maintainable in isolated northern locations. Many DND/CAF sites exist in remote areas or within small Arctic communities that have limited or no road access and must be reached by alternative means of transportation such as barges or heavy-lift aircraft. Consequently, new systems must feature modular designs that can be transported and assembled on site with minimal heavy-lift equipment by non-technicians using commonly available tools. To ensure sustained operation, proposed solutions should use readily available parts, be serviceable by local tradespeople, and operate with minimal human intervention once deployed. Essential Outcomes The proposed solution must: • Provide a design for a wind-powered electrical generation system in the 25–100 kW range, incorporating details of the structural, mechanical, electrical, and control elements required. • Provide integration and operational demonstration plan(s), showing how the wind-powered electric generator system can function in remote northern locations and operate and withstand northern environmental conditions, including extreme cold (down to –60 °C), high winds (up to 120 km/h), and icing conditions without intervention. • Integrate with existing electrical power systems or microgrids and must enable coordinated operation with other energy sources and support performance under varying generation and load conditions. • Use a modular design that allows transport by air or ship — ensuring that individual components fit within a standard 20ft sea container with maximum dimensions of 108 in. (2.74 m) wide × 268 in. (6.81 m) long × 96 in. (2.44 m) high and a maximum weight of 24,000 lb (10,886 kg; 10.9 tonnes). • The modular design must enable onsite assembly without the need for heavy lift equipment. • Support maintainability and repairability in northern environments by ensuring the wind powered electric generator system can be serviced using standard mechanical and electrical tools, without reliance on specialized proprietary equipment or manufacturer field support. Desired Outcomes Proposed solutions should include capabilities such as, but not limited to, the following: • Electromagnetic interference that complies with MIL STD 461G, Department of Defense Interface Standard for the Control of Electromagnetic Interference Characteristics of Subsystems and Equipment. • Foundation design that accounts for Arctic ground conditions, including permafrost, active-layer variation, and freeze-thaw effects, over the intended design life of the generator.

title: RF Data Fusion for Command and Control
description: This Challenge notice is issued under the Innovation for Defence Excellence and Security (IDEaS) Program Call for Proposals (CFP) Call 006 (W7714-248676/A). Solicitation Documents reference: See bidding details section. *For additional general information on the IDEaS Program, visit: https://www.canada.ca/en/department-national-defence/programs/defence-ideas.html _____________ This challenge is open to receive proposals for Component 1a, Component 1b and Component 2. Proposed solutions that fall within technology readiness levels (TRL) 1-9 can be submitted to this challenge. Steps to apply: Step 1: read this challenge Step 2: read the Call for Proposals : See bidding details section Step 3: propose your solution here : https://defence-innovation-portal.my.site.com/ _____________ Maximum Funding and Performance Period Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge. The individual maximum contract funding available under Component 1a (TRL 1-3) is up to $250,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of up to 6 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 1b (TRL 4-5) is up to $1,500,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of 12 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 2 (TRL 6-9) is up to $5,000,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes). The period of performance will be determined at the time of contract negotiation. The maximum individual contractual funding and the maximum performance period offered under Component 3 will be determined by Canada at the time of contract negotiation. This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to contract for the total approximate funding. _____________ Challenge Details Challenge Title: W7714-248676/017 - RF Data Fusion for Command and Control The Department of National Defence (DND) and the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) are seeking innovative software-based solutions to seamlessly convert, analyze, and fuse real-time, domain-specific, content-rich data transmitted over radio frequency (RF) bearers into a secure, standardized pan-domain Command and Control (C2) format to enhance interoperability and enable timely, data-driven decision-making across all domains and levels of command. Background and context Radio frequency (RF) communications in military operations are inherently bandwidth-constrained and vulnerable to jamming, interference, and environmental effects, making them unreliable in contested environments. To maintain timely and effective support across all warfighting domains, data transmitted over RF bearers should be transformed into compact, structured messages, such as eXtensible Markup Language (XML)-based Message Text Formats (MTF) or other machine-readable schemas. Such messages should be optimized for transmission over tactical networks including Low Frequency (LF), Very Low Frequency (VLF), High Frequency (HF), Ultra High Frequency (UHF), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM). This approach enables resilient, standards-based communication across domains (land, air, maritime, cyber, and space) and functional services (e.g., Joint Intelligence Surveillance and Reconnaissance (JISR), medical, logistics), in line with doctrinal requirements for pan-domain operations. CAF tactical messaging remains largely dependent on legacy systems. These systems are inflexible, poorly suited to machine-to-machine exchange, and increasingly misaligned with NATO’s shift toward XML-based, data-centric frameworks. CAF operators currently lack integrated, machine-readable messaging systems. As a result, they must manually convert voice, chat, and text inputs into formal military products including orders, situation reports, and Requests for Information (RFIs) to comply with command structures and coalition standards. Modern, pan-domain operations require that doctrinal and technical Information Exchange Requirements (IERs) be met at the speed of operational relevance, with messaging that is interoperable, standardized, and capable of supporting real-time, data-driven decision-making in joint and coalition environments. As NATO, the U.S. Department of Defense, and other Five Eyes partners adopt XML-based, machine-readable messaging frameworks, the CAF is prioritizing alignment with these emerging data models to improve interoperability, operational agility, and mission effectiveness. The DND/CAF are seeking innovative, interoperable, and scalable solutions that will contribute to the development of a next-generation digital military RF messaging and data exchange. Innovators are invited to propose technologies, platforms, or integrated systems. Essential Outcomes The proposed solution must: • Be a software-based capability (e.g., standalone application, plug-in, middleware, or service). • Support DND/CAF operations across all domains (land, air, maritime, space, cyber) and functional services (e.g., C2, intelligence, logistics). • Implement structured, standards-compliant messaging (e.g., MTF-XML) and data exchange protocols (e.g., National Information Exchange Model (NIEM), NATO Core Data Framework (NCDF)), with documented interfaces for importing, exporting, and exchanging data using those standards. • Be configurable and modular, supporting Character-Oriented Information Exchange (COIE) processing and designed for future extensibility (e.g., to accommodate emerging or disruptive standards). • Provide documented interfaces and standards-based data exchange mechanisms to support system integration, including use within experimentation, simulation, and wargaming environments. Desired Outcomes The proposed solution should include capabilities such as, but not limited to, the following: • Operability in Denied, Degraded, Intermittent, and Low Bandwidth (DDIL) environments, with scalability to support evolving mission requirements and force structures. • Enhanced user experience features such as intuitive interfaces, multilingual support, automation of routine workflows, and built-in decision aids. • Standardized, documented integration interfaces (e.g., application programming interfaces (APIs)) to enable integration with at least one Service Management or Service Monitoring tools or platforms (e.g., ServiceNow, Splunk, Dynatrace, Microsoft System Center, Azure Monitor, etc.). • Readiness for future integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) capabilities to support data fusion, intelligent message prioritization, and real-time decision support.

The maximum individual contractual funding and the maximum performance period offered under Component 3 will be determined by Canada at the time of contract negotiation. This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to contract for the total approximate funding. _____________ Challenge Details Challenge Title: W7714-248676/018 - Sustainable Northern Operations: Water & Waste The Department of National Defence and the Canadian Armed Forces (DND/CAF) are seeking novel, integrated technologies that enable the CAF to operate Relocatable Transportable Camps (RTCs) independently and sustainably in Arctic and sub-Arctic environments while meeting all applicable Canadian environmental and health regulations. Background and context The CAF’s strategic update Our North, Strong and Free (2024) directs an expansion of military operations in the Canadian North. RTCs deployed in remote Arctic regions must sustain personnel with safe water, sanitation, and waste-handling capabilities while minimizing logistics and environmental risk. In 2023, the IDEaS Pop-Up City contest demonstrated advanced, containerized power-water-waste systems. These prototypes significantly reduced solid-waste mass and potable-water demand but were not tested under Arctic winter conditions. Material brittleness, freezing of fluids, and power-efficiency issues remain key obstacles. This challenge will bridge this gap by developing, and then testing integrated cold-weather water and waste technologies under Arctic winter conditions (e.g., Op NANOOK). The objective of the challenge is to support the development of a proven, deployable, Canadian-made, Arctic-ready water-and-waste system enabling CAF RTCs to operate independently, safely, and sustainably in the North with drastically reduced logistics burden and environmental impact. Essential outcomes Proposed solutions must meet the following requirements: • Integrated capability combining water purification, wastewater treatment and solid-waste reduction suitable for camps of up to 50 personnel. • Use a modular design that allows transport by air or ship – ensuring that individual components fit within a standard 20 ft sea container with maximum dimensions of 108 in. (2.74 m) wide × 268 in. (6.81 m) long × 96 in. (2.44 m) high and a maximum weight of 24,000 lb (10,886 kg; 10.9 tonnes). The modular design must also enable on site assembly without the need for heavy lift equipment. • Treated outputs must meet or exceed Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and Health Canada Drinking-Water Guidelines. • Function continuously in remote northern locations and operate and withstand northern environmental conditions, including extreme cold down to -40°C. • Resource efficiency must be demonstrated through a reduction in resupply volume and frequency (fuel, water, consumables) by at least 75% from baseline (see Table 1 below). • Support maintainability and repairability in northern environments by ensuring that the solution can be serviced using common trades and tools available to CAF in deployed operations in remote areas. Desired outcomes Proposed solutions should include capabilities such as, but not limited to, the following: • Integrated power. • Operable in extreme heat conditions (up to +40°C). • No manual pre-processing of solid waste. • Recovery and reuse of waste-heat or by-products. • Can be scaled to suit camps of over 50 personnel, up to 1500 personnel. title: Natchez Trace Parkway Project MS NP NATR 3F26
description: Sealed bids from all business concerns will be accepted for the Natchez Trace Parkway, Project MS NP NATR 3F26, Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000001, located in Chickasaw County, Mississippi. The project consists of resurfacing the Parkway, including ramps, bridges, intersections and parking/pull-off areas. The work includes milling, asphalt overlay, shoulder widening, spot reconstruction, pavement markings, raised profile striping at bridge approaches, and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost of the entire project expected to fall within the price range of $10,000,000 to $12,000,000. title: Netherlands – Supply services of personnel including temporary staff – Inhuur flexwerkers voor diverse Midwaste-leden
description: Aanbestedende dienst CV Midwaste Milieu UA (Midwaste) Poortweg 4 B 2612PA Delft Opdrachtgevers De Opdrachtgevers in deze aanbesteding zijn: - Afvalcombinatie 'De Vallei' Gemeenten BV - Afvalstoffendienst 's-Hertogenbosch - Regionaal Reinigingsbedrijf Avalex Den Haag - Dar NV Nijmegen - De Meerlanden Holding NV Rijsenhout - Saver NV Roosendaal Opdrachtomschrijving: Deze aanbesteding betreft een Europese openbare procedure voor de inhuur van flexwerkers ten behoeve van diverse leden van Midwaste. De opdracht omvat het ter beschikking stellen van flexwerkers, waarbij de aard, omvang en duur van de inzet kunnen verschillen per deelnemend Midwaste-lid. De specifieke kenmerken en behoeften worden nader toegelicht per perceel. Binnen deze aanbesteding zijn verschillende cao's van toepassing, afhankelijk van het betreffende Midwaste-lid. Opdrachtnemer houdt bij de uitvoering van de overeenkomst rekening met de voor het betreffende Midwaste-lid geldende cao en past, voor zover wettelijk en contractueel van toepassing, de daaruit voortvloeiende arbeidsvoorwaarden toe. Indien sprake is van overname van personeel, wordt verwacht dat de overgenomen medewerkers aansluiten bij de functie-indeling en loonschalen zoals deze binnen het betreffende Midwaste-lid worden gehanteerd. Doel van de opdracht: Met deze aanbesteding beogen de opdrachtgevers per perceel een duurzame samenwerking aan te gaan met een professionele dienstverlener die flexibel kan voorzien in de personeelsbehoefte van de deelnemende Midwaste-leden. Duur raamovereenkomst: De raamovereenkomsten treden in werking op 1 februari 2027 en hebben een initiële looptijd van twee jaar. Opdrachtgever heeft vervolgens de mogelijkheid de raamovereenkomsten viermaal (4) met een periode van twaalf (12) maanden te verlengen. Voor perceel 3 Afvalstoffendienst 's-Hertogenbosch geldt hierop een uitzondering: voor dit perceel bedraagt de verlengingsmogelijkheid tweemaal (2) een periode van twaalf (12) maanden.

title: Netherlands – Sewage, refuse, cleaning and environmental services – Europese openbare aanbesteding Bestrijden milieucalamiteiten en dumpingen op land en water
description: Europese openbare aanbesteding Bestrijden milieucalamiteiten en dumpingen op land en water. WSRL wil één aanspreekpunt voor milieucalamiteiten en dumpingen. Door het maken van duidelijke afspraken, wordt op eenduidige wijze met het bestrijden van milieucalamiteiten en dumpingen omgegaan. Opdrachtomschrijving De opdracht betreft het op afroep opruimen, inzamelen, transporteren, (laten) opslaan en (laten) verwerken van milieuverontreinigende stoffen en dumpingen op land en water in beheer in het beheergebied van WSRL, bij: Wegen en wegbermen (in Alblasserwaard en Vijfheerenlanden); Waterkeringen; Terreinen in eigendom van WSRL; Watergangen/-vaarwegen. Milieuverontreinigende stoffen zijn stoffen die schade kunnen toebrengen aan de leefomgeving, mens en/of milieu, bijvoorbeeld chemicaliën, oliën (inclusief brandstoffen) en asbestdeeltjes. Dumpingen zijn afvalstoffen die onbeheerd worden aangetroffen, bewust of onbewust (bijvoorbeeld bij een ongeval). Indien sprake is van (water)bodemverontreiniging dient Opdrachtnemer een milieukundig (water)bodemadvies (situationeel inclusief het nemen van waterkwaliteit monsters) uit te brengen waaruit blijkt of sanering op de calamiteitenlocatie noodzakelijk is. Mocht dat aan de orde zijn, dan draagt Opdrachtnemer zorg voor de uitvoering van de sanering. Indien Opdrachtnemer hier zelf niet voor erkend is, schakelt Opdrachtnemer een erkend onderaannemer hiervoor in. Opdrachtnemer is verantwoordelijk voor het eindresultaat. Het is van belang voor WSRL 24/7 – 365 dagen te beschikken over een gecontracteerde en daarmee gegarandeerde inzet van een Opdrachtnemer voor uitvoering van deze aanbestedingsopdracht. Na de melding van een calamiteit, verwacht WSRL van Inschrijver: 1. Door het stellen van de juiste vragen (doorvragen) aan de melder het zo volledig mogelijk inschatten van de situatie en bepalen van de te nemen maatregelen en in te zetten materieel en personeel; 2. Inschrijver neemt maatregelen om verdere verontreiniging, vervolgschade, uitbreiding en/of ecologische risico’s (risico’s ten aanzien van de leefomgeving, mens en milieu) van de calamiteit te voorkomen (De ter plaatse zijnde medewerker(s) van WSRL (meestal een handhaver) voeren vaak al kleine werkzaamheden uit, zoals oliebooms plaatsen op het water e.d.); 3. Het zorgdragen voor een veilige (verkeers)situatie en werkomgeving. Als het zelfstandig bestrijden van de calamiteit onmogelijk blijkt, moet Inschrijver de calamiteitlocatie alleen veiligstellen tot dat hulpdiensten en/of (andere) gespecialiseerde partijen ter plaatse zijn; 4. Indien de situatie hier om vraagt, voert Opdrachtnemer bij een spoedeisend karakter een milieukundig (water)bodemadvies en bodemsanering uit. Bij geen spoedeisend karakter heeft Opdrachtgever de mogelijkheid via een andere partij deze dienst af te nemen. Van Opdrachtnemer wordt in dat geval geen onderzoek of handeling daartoe vereist (zoals bijvoorbeeld het opstellen van de rapportage). Van spoedeisend karakter is sprake als (de kans op) milieuverontreiniging groter wordt; 5. Het uitvoeren van de werkzaamheden zo snel mogelijk afhandelen zodat het verkeer weer veilig en ongehinderd haar weg kan vervolgen; 6. Indien nodig uitvoeren van spoedeisende herstelwerkzaamheden aan/op de calamiteitenlocatie; 7. Situationeel leveren van schone grond (is grond en bodem dat volgens de huidige wetgeving mag worden toegepast); 8. Het op de juiste wijze afvoeren, transporteren, laten (opslaan) en (laten) verwerken van de milieuverontreinigende stoffen; 9. Opmaken van een opdrachtbevestiging over de calamiteit (24 uurs melding), milieukundig bodemadvies en/of rapportage bij (drugs)dumpingen; 10. Opdrachtgever gedurende de calamiteit en nazorg informeren over de uit te voeren/uitgevoerde calamiteitenbestrijding. Niet binnen de scope behoort: Het verwijderen van explosief en radioactief afval; Opdrachtgever voert het verhalen van schades op de verzekering van deze aanbestedingsopdracht zelf uit. Optioneel is het mogelijk de Raamovereenkomst met een periode van tweemaal (2) één (1) jaar te verlengen onder gelijkblijvende voorwaarden. WSRL bepaalt uiteindelijk of de Raamovereenkomst al dan niet wordt verlengd. Tevens heeft WSRL de mogelijkheid de Raamovereenkomst eenzijdig te beëindigen. Het beëindigen van de Raamovereenkomst is door WSRL mogelijk als bij evaluatie herhaaldelijk blijkt dat Opdrachtnemer gemaakte afspraken niet naleeft en/of afgesproken kwaliteit niet levert. De Raamovereenkomst heeft daardoor een maximale looptijd van vier (4) jaar en eindigt, zonder dat opzegging vereist is, van rechtswege na het verstrijken van de vier (4) jaar. De ingangsdatum van de Raamovereenkomst is 1 december 2026 of zoveel eerder of later dat Opdrachtgever en Opdrachtnemer overeenkomen.

title: Switzerland – Public utilities – IWB, Bereitstellung von Dienstleistungen für NES-Systemsoftware (SIP-Platinum)
description: Aktuell hat IWB 84 000 Smartmeter im Einsatz. IWB wird diese Anzahl kontinuierlich erweitern, um dem vorgegebenen Ziel der Gesetzgebung gerecht zu werden. Um diese Geräte zu betreiben, wird eine Software eingesetzt, die laufend weiterentwickelt wird, mit dem Ziel der Verbesserung und Korrektur vorhandener sowie der Erweiterung mit neuen Funktionen, die sich von Anregungen und Wünschen der Praxis, von sich ändernden Systemumgebungen (aktualisierte Systemsoftware etc.) bzw. von gesetzlichen Rahmenbedingungen ableiten. Daher muss die Software regelmässig aktualisiert werden. Bei IWB steht die Software des Lieferanten NES im Einsatz. Die Aktualisierungen der Software (siehe Anhang C1 «SIP Datasheet») werden von NES jedoch nicht direkt an die Versorger, sondern ausschliesslich über Reseller, sogenannte Development-Partner, ausgeliefert. Die Firma NES bietet für die NES-Systemsoftware, für NES Softwaretools und die zugehörigen NES-Komponenten (Datenkonzentratoren, Zähler, Lastschaltgeräte, OSGP-Endgeräte) umfangreichen Support an. Mit dem Software Investment Protection (SIP) Platinum Service werden sämtliche Weiterentwicklungen und Systemverbesserungen abgedeckt. Die NES Wartung (SIP Service Platinum) beinhaltet Software und Firmware Updates innerhalb der gleichen Releases sowie Upgrades auf weitere Releases für Zähler, DC/DCN und NES System Software (Head End System), NES Provisioning Tool und NES Diagnostics Tool sowie Telefon und Web basierenden technischen Support. Aufgrund der bei IWB eingesetzten Software ist «SIP Platinum» oder gleichwertig erforderlich. IWB benötigt einen Reseller, der uns die Systemanpassungen gemäss SIP Platinum auf einem von IWB definierten Datenübergabepunkt für die kommenden vier Jahre (2027-2030) zur Verfügung stellt.

description: Postępowanie prowadzone jest zgodnie z przepisami ustawy z dnia 11 września 2019 r. Prawo zamówień publicznych (Dz.U. z 2026 r. poz. 793) zwana dalej ustawą Pzp. Przedmiotem zamówienia jest dostawa przetworów warzywnych kwaszonych. Kod Wspólnego Słownika Zamówień (CPV): 15331000-7 Warzywa przetworzone Szczegółowy opis przedmiotu zamówienia określają załączniki nr 1, 1.1., 5 oraz nr 4 do SWZ tj.: Formularz ofertowy, Specyfikacja asortymentowo - cenowa, Opisy przedmiotów zamówienia oraz Projektowane postanowienia umowy. Zamawiający nie dopuszcza składanie ofert częściowych. Uzasadnienie: Zamawiający nie dopuszcza składania ofert częściowych, ponieważ przedmiot zamówienia obejmuje sukcesywne dostawy przetworów warzywnych kwaszonych, które wymagają zapewnienia ciągłości dostaw, jednolitego poziomu jakości oraz sprawnej organizacji i koordynacji realizacji zamówienia. Podział zamówienia na części i powierzenie ich realizacji kilku wykonawcom mógłby utrudnić bieżącą koordynację dostaw, w szczególności w zakresie terminów, ilości oraz jakości dostarczanych produktów. W przypadku wystąpienia braków, opóźnień lub konieczności wymiany produktów konieczne byłoby dodatkowe uzgadnianie działań pomiędzy Zamawiającym a poszczególnymi Wykonawcami, co mogłoby negatywnie wpłynąć na ciągłość zaopatrzenia. Ponadto dostawy realizowane przez różnych Wykonawców mogłyby wiązać się z różnicami w jakości oraz sposobie realizacji dostaw, co utrudniałoby zapewnienie jednolitych standardów wymaganych przez Zamawiającego. Podział zamówienia mógłby również powodować zwiększenie kosztów organizacyjnych i logistycznych, związanych m.in. z obsługą kilku umów, koordynacją wielu dostaw oraz kontrolą ich prawidłowej realizacji. Z uwagi na powyższe Zamawiający uznaje, że realizacja całości zamówienia przez jednego Wykonawcę zapewni sprawniejszą organizację dostaw, większą ciągłość i przewidywalność zaopatrzenia oraz jednolity standard jakości dostarczanych przetworów warzywnych kwaszonych, a także pozwoli ograniczyć koszty i ryzyka związane z koordynacją współpracy z wieloma Wykonawcami. Zamawiający wymaga złożenia oferty na wszystkie wymagane pozycje wykazane w załącznikach nr 1.1. do SWZ. Zamawiający w niniejszym postępowaniu przewiduje udzielenie zamówienia podstawowego (gwarantowanego) oraz ewentualnych zamówień w ramach Prawa Opcji. Informacje dotyczące zakresu zamówienia objętego Prawem Opcji, w tym zakres, termin skorzystania z tego uprawnienia przez Zamawiającego oraz zasady, na jakich będzie się to odbywało, zostały opisane w załączniku nr 4 do SWZ. Prawo Opcji jest uprawnieniem Zamawiającego, z którego może, ale nie musi, skorzystać w ramach niniejszego postępowania. Zamawiający nie ponosi żadnej odpowiedzialności z tytułu nieskierowania takiego żądania do Wykonawcy, a Wykonawcy z tytułu nie skorzystania z Prawa Opcji przez Zamawiającego nie przysługuje żadne roszczenie. Okoliczności skorzystania z opcji zostały opisane w § 3 w załączniku nr 4 do SWZ. Ilekroć w niniejszej SWZ przedmiot zamówienia jest opisany ze wskazaniem znaków towarowych, patentów lub pochodzenia, źródła lub szczególnego procesu, który charakteryzuje produkty dostarczane przez konkretnego Wykonawcę, jeżeli mogłoby to doprowadzić do uprzywilejowania lub wyeliminowania niektórych wykonawców lub produktów, to przyjmuje się, że wskazaniom takim towarzyszą wyrazy „lub równoważne”. Zamawiający, opisując przedmiot zamówienia, na podstawie dyspozycji wyrażonej w art. 99 ust. 4 ustawy Pzp, wskazał na znak towarowy lub pochodzenie z uwagi na specyfikę przedmiotu zamówienia oraz brak możliwości jego opisania w sposób wyczerpujący za pomocą dokładnych i zrozumiałych określeń. Opisując przedmiot zamówienia za pomocą znaków towarowych, patentów lub pochodzenia, źródła lub szczególnego procesu, który charakteryzuje produkty dostarczane Zamawiający określa tym samym parametry jakościowe, techniczne i cechy użytkowe, jakim musi odpowiadać przedmiot zamówienia, aby spełniać wymagania stawiane przez Zamawiającego. Przedmiot zamówienia powinien odpowiadać określonym przez Zamawiającego parametrom technicznym, funkcjonalnym i jakościowym wskazanym w opisie przedmiotu zamówienia, stanowiącym załącznik nr 5 do SWZ. title: Bulgaria – Organisation of architectural design contests – Открит архитектурен конкурс за идеен проект – „Преустройство и ревитализация на пешеходен подлез „Тримонциум“ и прилежаща градска територия", гр. Пловдив
description: Предмет на настоящата обществена поръчка е изработването на идеен проект за преустройство и ревитализация на пешеходен подлез „Тримонциум“ и прилежаща градска територия, с териториален обхват: подземно пространство + надземни подходи и прилежащи публични пространства. Обхвата на разработката включва пешеходен подлез „Тримонциум“ представляващ ПИ 56784.521.1382 и ПИ 56784.523.4022, находящ се в гр. Пловдив, район „Централен“, бул. „Цар Борис III Обединител“. Конкурсът се провежда с цел придобиване на идеен проект – база за възлагане на последващо проектиране в техническа фаза. Общата прогнозна стойност на конкурса за проект е 255 500 евро без ДДС и е определена по реда на чл. 80, ал. 3 ЗОП като сбор от наградите и прогнозната стойност на обществената поръчка за услуга, която може да бъде възложена чрез процедура на договаряне без предварително обявление. Окончателните технически, финансови и договорни условия, включително цената за изпълнение, ще бъдат предмет на преговори в последващата процедура. Предвиждането на последващото договаряне не създава безусловно задължение за възложителя да сключи договор. Договор се сключва при постигане на съгласие по условията на изпълнение и при осигурено финансиране. С участието си в настоящия конкурс участниците, получили награди, изрично се съгласяват, че при отказ от страна на класираните на първо и второ място участници да участват в процедурата по реда на чл. 79, ал. 1, т. 9 от ЗОП, или в случай, че процедурата на договаряне без предварително обявление не приключи със сключване на договор за обществена поръчка, Възложителят има право да проведе процедура по избор на изпълнител за изработване на инвестиционен проект във фази „технически“ и „работен“ проект, като използва техните концептуални проекти. Наградените проекти са произведения, създадени по поръчка по смисъла на чл. 42 от Закона за авторското право и сродните му права. След изплащане на наградите по сметките на участниците, посочени в заявленията, за възложителя възниква правото да използва проектите на класираните участници без разрешението на участниците и без да дължи допълнително възнаграждение за това. Общия размер на наградния фонд е 30 000 евро без ДДС, разпределен както следва: I-ва награда: 15 000 € (петнадесет хиляди евро) и предвидена възможност за последващо възлагане на изработването на технически и работен инвестиционен проект чрез процедура на договаряне без предварително обявление по чл. 79, ал. 1, т. 13 от Закона за обществените поръчки, при условията на действащото българско законодателство и при наличие на осигурено финансиране. II-ра награда: 8000 € (осем хиляди евро). III-та награда: 5000 € (пет хиляди евро). Две поощрителни награди от 1000 € (хиляда евро) по преценка на журито. title: IWB, Provision of Services for NES System Software (SIP-Platinum)
description:
IWB currently has 84,000 smart meters in use. IWB will continue to increase this number to meet the legislative requirements.


To operate these devices, software is used that is continuously being developed with the goal of improving and correcting existing functions, as well as adding new ones derived from practical suggestions and requests, changing system environments (updated system software, etc.), and legal requirements. Therefore, the software must be updated regularly. IWB uses software from the supplier NES. However, software updates (see Appendix C1 “SIP Datasheet”) are not delivered directly by NES to the utilities but exclusively through resellers, known as development partners. NES offers comprehensive support for NES system software, NES software tools, and the associated NES components (data concentrators, meters, load switching devices, OSGP terminals). The Software Investment Protection (SIP) Platinum Service covers all future developments and system enhancements. NES maintenance (SIP Service Platinum) includes software and firmware updates within the same releases, as well as upgrades to subsequent releases for meters, DC/DCN, and NES system software (Head End System), the NES Provisioning Tool, and the NES Diagnostics Tool, along with telephone and web-based technical support. Due to the software used at IWB, “SIP Platinum” or an equivalent service is required.


IWB requires a reseller who will provide us with the system customizations in accordance with SIP Platinum at a data transfer point defined by IWB for the next four years (2027–2030).

title: IWB, Servers and Virtualization Infrastructure
description:
Over the coming years, as part of the product lifecycle of the client-server infrastructure, IWB will replace or upgrade various components on a rolling basis and carry out necessary expansions and upgrades.


This request for proposals covers servers and virtualization infrastructure components.


The request for proposals is divided into two lots:


Lot 1: Server systems (compatible with the existing HP infrastructure), including maintenance


Lot 2: Virtualization software licenses (VMware and Omnissa Horizon)


Lot 1: The systems supplied must be compatible with the existing HP server infrastructure and the existing VMware infrastructure. The objective of this request for proposals for Lot 1 is to enter into a framework agreement with three vendors for a period of three years. The prices quoted for Lot 1 are valid until at least March 31, 2027. When a specific need arises, the successful bidders will be asked to submit their respective bids as part of a mini-tender. IWB will award the corresponding individual contract to the contractor offering the highest discount off the manufacturer’s price list.


Lot 2: The objective of this request for proposals for Lot 2 is to enter into a three-year framework service agreement with one provider for the procurement of virtualization licenses.

title: Schulreinigung
description: Der Auftraggeber überträgt dem Auftragnehmer die Ausführung von Unterhalts-, Grund-, Glas- und Rahmenreinigungsarbeiten sowie bedarfsgerechten Sondereinigungsarbeiten, Stellung und Wechseln von Schmutzfangmatten für Schulen des Bezirksamtes Steglitz-Zehlendorf von Berlin. Der zu schließende Vertrag umfasst regelmäßige Unterhaltsreinigungsarbeiten im Tages- und Abendbetrieb sowie regelmäßige und unregelmäßige, bedarfsgerechte Sonderreinigungsarbeiten, eine jährliche Grundreinigung sowie eine jährliche Glas- und Rahmenreinigung. Weiterhin umfasst der Vertrag auch für bestimmte Liegenschaften die Stellung und den regelmäßigen Wechsel von Schmutzfangmatten. Der Bieter wird darauf hingewiesen, dass nur für die Lose ein Angebot abgegeben werden darf, die der tatsächlichen Leistungsfähigkeit des Bieters auch unter Berücksichtigung der Zeitspanne zwischen Angebotsabgabe und Vertragsbeginn entspricht. Sofern der Auftraggeber während der Prüfung und Wertungsphase des Angebotes feststellt, dass das Angebot nicht der Leistungsfähigkeit des Bieters entspricht, wird das gesamte Angebot von der weiteren Wertung ausgeschlossen. Die vergaberechtliche Leistungsfähigkeit vorausgesetzt, kann jeder Bieter maximal für 2 - zwei - Lose ein Angebot abgeben und maximal für zwei Lose einen Zuschlag erhalten, sofern er hierfür das wirtschaftlichste Angebot abgegeben hat. Besichtigungstermine Um eine Fehlkalkulation zu vermeiden, empfiehlt der Auftraggeber dringend die Besichtigung aller Objekte vor Abgabe des Angebots. In der Vergangenheit führten Reinigungsmängel bei mehreren Gebäuden zu Vertragsstrafen. Eine Besichtigung stellt sicher, dass alle baulichen Besonderheiten bekannt sind und die Kosten vertragskonform kalkuliert werden können. Der Bieter hat dem Auftraggeber über die Vergabeplattform die Objekte, die er besichtigen möchte, bis zum 25.09.2026 schriftlich zu benennen. Die Vergabestelle wird dann eine Liste der zuständigen Ansprechpartner in den jeweiligen Einrichtungen übermitteln. Die Besichtigungen sind bis zum 09.10.2026 mit dem jeweiligen Ansprechpartner vor Ort zu vereinbaren. Der Bieter wird aufgefordert, sich an die vereinbarten Terminvorgaben zu halten, damit unnötige Störungen des Dienstbetriebes in den Objekten vermieden werden.

description: Konkurransen gjelder levering av en løsning for kjøp og administrasjon av digitale læreverk, læremidler, læringsressurser og produksjonsverktøy – heretter samlet omtalt som digitale læremidler. Anskaffelsen omfatter også en webløsning for bestilling, oversikt og administrasjon av lisenser. Løsningen håndterer rapporter og statistikk som viser både kjøp av lisenser og faktisk bruk av lisensene. Oppdragsgiver har behov for at løsningen leveres som en løpende tjeneste. Anskaffelsens verdi anslås til over EØS terskelverdi. Volumet er et estimat og er ikke bindende for oppdragsgiver. For nærmere informasjon viser vi til anskaffelsesdokumentene. Oppdragsgiver tar forbehold om avlysning av konkurransen, blant annet i forbindelse med budsjettmessig dekning. Denne anskaffelsen er etter sin art vurdert til å ha en uvesentlig innvirkning på klima og miljø, jf. anskaffelsesloven § 5b tredje ledd. Begrunnelsen for dette er at anskaffelsen gjelder kjøp av løsning for kjøp og administrasjon av digitale læremidler, der anskaffelsens art medfører at oppdragsgiver er avskåret fra å påvirke klima og miljøpåvirkningen, siden krav og kriterier som retter seg mot disse elementene ikke vil ha tilstrekkelig tilknytning til leveransen, jf. DFØs miljøveileder. Plikten til å stille krav om lærling er vurdert til å gjelde for denne anskaffelsen, jf. anskaffelsesloven § 5h. Se kontrakten for mer informasjon.

description: Team Danmarks organisation består af en administrerende direktør, en sportsdirektør og ca. 50 medarbejdere, som arbejder inden for syv sportsfaglige områder: Sportsligt samarbejde, karriere- og talentudvikling, sportsmedicin, sportsfysiologi, analyse, ernæring og psykologi. Team Danmarks vision er at skabe de bedst mulige vilkår og rammer for dansk eliteidræt og for de enkelte atleter. At udvikle eliteidræt i verdensklasse handler således for Team Danmark om at sikre en rød tråd gennem atletens rejse – fra klubben, hvor det hele starter, hele vejen til toppen af medaljeskamlen og videre til livet efter sportskarrieren. Det handler både om mennesker og medaljer. For at kunne udleve denne vision er det afgørende, at Team Danmarks atleter og trænere har adgang til træningsudstyr af høj kvalitet, der understøtter optimal træning, restitution og præstation på højeste internationale niveau. Team Danmark ønsker således med dette udbud at indkøbe træningsudstyr, som netop skal bidrage til at sikre de danske eliteatleter de bedst mulige fysiske rammer og vilkår for at udvikle og udleve deres fulde potentiale inden for et samlet budget på 8 mio. kr. ekskl. moms. På denne baggrund udbyder Team Danmark følgende tre ikke eksklusive delkontrakter, der alle udbydes som rammeaftaler for en 4-årig periode, men hvor den leverandør, der tildeles den enkelte delkontrakt, er garanteret et engangsindkøb, der foretages af Team Danmark umiddelbart efter indgåelsen af den relevante delkontrakt, og hvor det træningsudstyr, der omfattes af engangsindkøbet, skal leveres til Team Danmark senest i løbet af april 2027: (i) Delkontrakt A, der vedrører et engangsindkøb af cardioudstyr samt løbende indkøb af cardioudstyr med et maksimumbeløb på i alt 2,5 mio. kr. ekskl. moms (ii) Delkontrakt B, der vedrører et engangsindkøb af træningsmaskiner samt løbende indkøb af træningsmaskiner med et maksimumbeløb på i alt 2,5 mio. kr. ekskl. moms (iii) Delkontrakt C, der vedrører et engangsindkøb af stænger og frivægte samt løbende indkøb af stænger og frivægter med et maksimumbeløb på i alt 3 mio. kr. ekskl. moms. Det engangsindkøb, som Team Danmark forpligter sig til at foretage umiddelbart efter indgåelsen af den relevante delkontrakt, er nærmere defineret i tilbudslisten. Udover engangsindkøbet har Team Danmark ikke aftagepligt på hverken delkontrakt A, delkontrakt B eller delkontrakt C. Det forventet indkøbsbehov over de næste fire år er indsat i tilbudslisten til brug for evalueringen. Dette forventede indkøbsbehov er alene vejledende og baseret på Team Danmarks skøn over det forventede indkøb og er således ikke bindende for Team Danmark. Dette betyder, at de(n) leverandør, der tildeles delkontrakt A og/eller delkontrakt B eller delkontrakt C, ikke kan gøre krav gældende mod Team Danmark, hvis Team Danmarks indkøbsbehov viser sig at være mindre end det, der er anført i tilbudslisten. Ligeledes skal leverandøren på hver delaftale kunne levere større mængder, end hvad der fremgår af det estimerede indkøb, idet der i alle tre delkontrakter er en bestemmelse om, at Team Danmark er berettiget til at forhøje delkontrakternes ramme med 50 % indtil seks måneder før delkontrakternes indkøbsperiodes udløb Opdelingen i tre delkontrakter er begrundet i, at markedet for henholdsvis cardio-udstyr (delkontrakt A), træningsmaskiner (delkontrakt B) samt stænger og frivægte (delkontrakt C) i vidt omfang består af forskellige og til dels specialiserede leverandører, hvorfor en opdeling giver flere virksomheder, herunder mindre og mere specialiserede leverandører, mulighed for at afgive tilbud på den eller de delkontrakter, der matcher deres forretningsområde. Opdelingen understøtter dermed konkurrencen om den enkelte delkontrakt og øger sandsynligheden for, at Team Danmark modtager konkurrencedygtige tilbud på samtlige tre produktkategorier. Tilbudsgiver kan afgive tilbud på alle delkontrakter. En tilbudsgiver kan tildeles delkontrakt A og delkontrakt B, men kan ikke samtidig tildeles delkontrakt C. Den tilbudsgiver, der tildeles delkontrakt C, kan således alene tildeles denne delkontrakt. Dette betyder, at tilbudsgiver, hvis tilbudsgiver tildeles delkontrakt C, ikke kan tildeles delkontrakt A og/eller delkontrakt B. Tildeles tilbudsgiver delkontrakt A, kan tilbudsgiver godt blive tildelt delkontrakt B. Tilsvarende kan tilbudsgiver godt blive tildelt delkontrakt B, hvis tilbudsgiver tildeles delkontrakt A. Delkontrakterne forventes at træde i kraft ved kontraktunderskrivelse og løber herefter i 48 måneder. De krav, der stilles til det træningsudstyr, der er omfattet af henholdsvis delkontrakt A, delkontrakt B og delkontrakt C, er nærmere beskrevet i kravsspecifikationen, der er vedlagt som en del af udbudsmaterialet. Tilbudsgiver skal stille en række vareprøver til rådighed for Team Danmark. De vareprøver, som tilbudsgiver skal stille til rådighed for Team Danmark, er markeret med grøn i tilbudslisten, der indgår som en del af det samlede udbudsmateriale. Udbuddet gennemføres elektronisk ved brug af udbudsportalen www.udbuddet.dk. Tilbudsgiver skal derfor oprettes som licenshaver hos www.udbuddet.dk. Oprettelse kan ske uden omkostning. Spørgsmål vedrørende www.udbuddet.dk skal stilles direkte til www.udbuddet.dk via support-funktionen, der kan træffes via telefon +45 7022 7007 Der ydes ikke vederlag for tilbudsgivernes deltagelse i udbudsprocessen. Hvis der nogetsteds i kravsspecifikationen eller udbudsmaterialet i øvrigt er henvist til standarder, skal enhver henvisning forstås som en henvisning til den nævnte standard eller tilsvarende. Opfylder tilbudsgiver ikke den nævnte standard, men tilsvarende, skal tilbudsgiver i tilbuddet dokumentere, at den tilbudte løsning på de relevante parametre er tilsvarende. I det tilfælde tilbudsgiverne fremsætter ønske om det, afholder Ordregiver gerne et infomøde forud for tilbudsfristen. Tilbudsgiverne opfordres i så fald til at tilkendegive ønsket herom på udbudsportalen.

description: Sources Sought: Euclid Creek Fishway Construction; W912P425X11LG SOURCES SOUGHT DESCRIPTION: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE, RELEASED PURSUANT TO FEDERAL ACQUISITION REGULATION (FAR) PART 10: MARKET RESEARCH. By way of this Market Survey/Sources Sought Notice, the USACE-Buffalo District intends to determine the extent of firms that are engaged in providing the services described hereunder for the Euclid Creek Fishway. This Sources Sought Notice is issued solely for informational, market research, and planning purposes only and does not commit the government to any further contract actions, i.e., solicitation and/or contract. Respondents are advised that the United States Government will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in responding to this Sources Sought Notice. Not responding to this Sources Sought Notice does not preclude participation in any future Request for Proposals (if any) that may be issued. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the U.S Government to form a binding contract. This is not a solicitation announcement; this is a Request for Information (RFI) only. This Notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP); it does not guarantee the future issue of an RFP; nor does it commit the government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Further, this Agency will not accept unsolicited proposals. Respondents are advised that this Agency will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in response to this Notice; all costs associated with responding to this Notice will be solely at the responding party's expense. At this time, proprietary information is not being requested, and respondents shall refrain from providing proprietary information in response to this Notice. Responses to this Notice will not be returned. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Not responding to this Notice does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the U.S Government to form a binding contract. It is the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this Notice. GOVERNMENT REQUIREMENTS: The purpose of this project is to construct a full width ramp with a series of 31 weirs and pools. These weirs are designed as an upstream-pointing arch with side slopes which concentrate the flow towards the center of the channel. Further design elements include a 4-foot-wide V-notch in the weir and 1.5-foot diameter boulders emplaced on the weir. The 31st weir (upstream most weir) will be constructed entirely of concrete the intent is to protect the less robust rock emplacements by breaking up incoming ice. Construction of the fishway will involve partial demolition and excavation of the spillway and underlying bedrock to anchor the fishway to the rock and replace the existing spillway. On the downstream end of the fishway the existing channel will be removed for a length of 150 feet. A four foot-wide embedded low-flow channel in the center of the fishway has been designed to provide sufficient depth of water and flow during normal low flow conditions to allow fish passage. A series of parallel transverse rock ridges that consist of 1�6� foot diameter stones will be evenly spaced along the length of the ramp to provide a series of pools and falls. This low-flow channel and rock ridges are designed to allow for the passage of fish and other aquatic life would occur. Contract duration is estimated at 10 months. The estimated cost range is between $1,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00. Each project must include the name, title, project role, e-mail address, and telephone number of at least one reference. References may be used to verify project size, scope, dollar value, percentages, and quality of performance. Example projects must be of similar size and scope. title: APN - New Facility and Compound, CFB Uplands
description: Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform the Design-Builder of an upcoming contract opportunity at CFB Uplands in Ottawa, Ontario. The purpose of this APN is to allow the Design-Builder to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested Design-Builders to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that this project will include an Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process.   Description of the Project and Services   This contract will provide the design and construction of the new facility and compound near the existing CETEMT compound at CFB Uplands. The new facility will be a single-storey building with an approximate footprint of 1,650 m2. It will include offices and workspaces, meeting rooms, maintenance garages and workshops, specialized spaces such as secure storage and a weapons vault, and support areas including a kitchenette, washrooms, and server rooms. The facility will be situated within a new exterior compound of approximately 6,500 m2, including parking areas.   ROM estimate for the total value of the contract is approximately $17M. It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND.   Contract Number: 88076 Title: CETEMT New Facility and Compound Approximate Estimate: $ 17M Anticipated Posting: Q4 FY26/27 Description: Provide the Counter Explosive Threat Equipment Management Team (CETEMT) a new facility and compound on CFB Uplands in Ottawa, Ontario according to operational requirements.   Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a Design-Builder will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated industrial security requirements of this project will be at FSC Secret. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing Design-Builders  early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, Design-Builders that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential Design-Builders with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, consultants or contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number (Project number on the MERX notice); Contract number 88076; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored for. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the consultants or contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a consultant or contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation (Contract number listed on their request for sponsorship) being advertised on MERX, has  met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package, and has submitted a proposal or a bid DCC will  send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or bidder regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent or bidder will need to promptly cooperate with CSP  to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca   Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Priscille Vumi Leader, Contract Services Defence Construction Canada 343-596-6289 Priscille.Vumi@dcc-cdc.gc.caBidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

Das ERZ betreibt an den Standorten Hagenholz und Werdhölzli eigene Personalrestaurants. 

Für die Sicherstellung eines reibungslosen Betriebes wird eine zuverlässige und kurzfristig 

verfügbare Personalvermittlung benötigt, die qualifiziertes Küchenpersonal gemäss den

betrieblichen Anforderungen zur Verfügung stellt. 


Wesentliche Punkte der erwarteten Leistung:


Der Anbieter verpflichtet sich, nach Anfrage innerhalb von 24 Stunden geeignetes Personal 

bereitzustellen. Die Einsatzdauer wird jeweils durch das ERZ definiert und kann von einem 

Tag bis zu mehreren Monaten variieren. 


Die ausgeschriebene Leistung umfasst: 


Rekrutierung und Bereitstellung von Küchenpersonal 

o Köche mit mindestens 2 Jahren Berufserfahrung oder EFZ-Abschluss, idealerweise mit Führungserfahrung 

o Hilfsköche mit mindestens 2 Jahren Berufserfahrung oder EBA-Abschluss 

o Küchenhilfen ohne Abschluss (Anfänger) nach Bedarf
